Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. You can use either the `gcloud` CLI (recommended for quick testing) or the raw REST API call if you prefer to embed it in your own automation. --- ## 1. Prerequisites | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **Enable APIs** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` | Needed for Compute Engine. | | **Set project** | `gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID` | All subsequent commands target this project. | | **Choose zone** | Pick a zone that supports GPUs, e.g. `us-central1-a`. | GPUs are only available in certain zones. | | **Create a service account** (if using REST) | `gcloud iam service-accounts create my-sa --display-name="Compute Service Account"`
`gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding YOUR_PROJECT_ID --member="serviceAccount:my-sa@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/compute.admin"` | Required for programmatic access. | | **Get credentials** (REST) | `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` | Use this token in the Authorization header. | > **Tip:** If you’re just experimenting, the `gcloud` CLI is the easiest path. The REST example below is useful if you’re building a custom deployment pipeline. --- ## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI ```bash # Variables PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID" ZONE="us-central1-a" INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu" MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed GPU_COUNT=1 GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000" IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts" IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud" # Create the instance gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \ --project="$PROJECT" \ --zone="$ZONE" \ --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \ --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \ --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \ --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \ --boot-disk-size=100GB \ --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \ --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \ --tags=http-server,https-server \ --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform ``` ### Optional: Startup Script (`startup.sh`) If you want to install NVIDIA drivers automatically: ```bash #!/bin/bash # Update package lists apt-get update # Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04) apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470 # Reboot to activate driver (optional) # reboot ``` > Save this script in the same directory as the `gcloud` command or provide an absolute path. --- ## 3. Using the REST API (JSON) Below is a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine API. Replace placeholders (`YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, etc.) with your actual values. ```json { "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu", "machineType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8", "disks": [ { "boot": true, "initializeParams": { "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts", "diskSizeGb": 100, "diskType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd" } } ], "networkInterfaces": [ { "network": "global/networks/default", "accessConfigs": [ { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" } ] } ], "accelerators": [ { "acceleratorCount": 1, "acceleratorType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000" } ], "metadata": { "items": [ { "key": "startup-script", "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470\n" } ] }, "tags": { "items": ["http-server", "https-server"] }, "serviceAccounts": [ { "email": "default", "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"] } ] } ``` ### Making the request ```bash TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token) curl -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d @instance.json \ "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances" ``` > Replace `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the payload above. --- ## 4. Verify the Instance After creation, you can check the status: ```bash gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a ``` Look for the `status` field (`PROVISIONING`, `STAGING`, `RUNNING`). Once it’s `RUNNING`, SSH into it: ```bash gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a ``` Inside the VM, verify the GPU: ```bash nvidia-smi ``` You should see an NVIDIA RTX A6000 listed. --- ## 5. Clean Up When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid ongoing charges: ```bash gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a ``` --- ### Summary - **CLI**: Quick, interactive, great for manual testing. - **REST**: Ideal for embedding in CI/CD pipelines or custom tooling. Both approaches use the same underlying Compute Engine API, so pick whichever fits your workflow. Happy GPU computing!
